newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Grand Coulee dam full; downstream flows up.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Grand Coulee dam full; downstream flows up.

text.p: The Grand Coulee dam in Mashington state has reached its reservoir target, resulting in higher flows through downstream hydroelectric projects, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates the dam, said Monday.
Grand Coulee has achieved its target elevation of 1,283 feet, said spokesman Craig Larsen.

Flows through the Chief Joseph hydroelectric dam, immediately downstream from Grand Coulee, are expected to average 110,000 to 120,000 cubic feet per second today, compared with 80,000 to 90,000 in the first week of October, he added.
"They are basically passing in-flow," Larsen said.

The Bonneville Power Administration, which markets power produced from federal dams in the Northwest, uses Chief Joseph as a "peaking" project, shaping most discharges into daytime, heavy load hours, he noted.

Grand Coulee receives in-flows from Canada, Northern Idaho and Montana. Downstream of Chief Joseph are five Mid-Columbia projects owned by a consortium of Washington public utility districts, followed by four other federal dams on the main stem of the Columbia river.
"There are ten dams effectively primed by Grand Coulee discharge," Larsen said.
